_comment: Vertical explainer: 1080x1920, graphics own the TOP half, the speaker owns the BOTTOM half, captions run in the MIDDLE band on the seam between them. The split is the format's whole argument - the viewer reads the graphic and hears the explanation without either one being decoration.
_usage: Project.create(root, slug, preset) deep-merges this over the skeleton in vedit/project.py: dicts merge, lists replace wholesale, project_id / created_utc / schema_version / _computed are dropped. Keys beginning with '_' are documentation and MUST be ignored by consumers.
name: shortform-explainer
description: 9:16 explainer. Graphics top half, speaker bottom half, captions in the middle band.
_comment_platform: Defaults to tiktok because it has the most restrictive safe area of the three vertical platforms - anything laid out for it is safe on Reels and Shorts. Retargeting is a one-line edit of output.platform plus a re-copy of that platform's loudnorm block from presets/platforms.json.
_comment_loudnorm: Copied from presets/platforms.json -> tiktok.loudnorm. Duplicated into the project on purpose: an already-mastered project must not silently re-target because platforms.json changed later. LRA 9 rather than 11 because the median listener is on a phone speaker in a noisy room, where wide dynamics just become inaudible passages.
_comment_bitrate: 256k and cq 21 rather than long form's 320k/20: the platform re-encodes this hard anyway, and a 60-second vertical clip gains nothing from the extra bits.
_comment_cut_profile: Short form earns the tighter thresholds - see presets/cut-profiles.json. Uncalibrated, like every other number in presets/.
_comment_captions: ON, always. The feed autoplays muted; without burned-in captions the first three seconds carry no information at all. Note the transcript may spell numerals as words (WhisperX runs with --suppress_numerals so that numerals cannot break word alignment), so '20' arrives as 'zwanzig' - fix it with a captions.overrides entry rather than by re-transcribing.

layout._comment: Regions are percentages of the output frame. The two halves meet exactly at y=50 %, and the caption band is centred on that seam, which is what stops the join from reading as a visible line.

graphics._comment_fit: contain, not cover: a graphic is information and must not be cropped. Anything left over shows the background colour.
graphics._comment_padding: top 8 % keeps the graphic clear of the platform's search and live badges - see platforms.tiktok.safe_area_pct.

speaker._comment_fit: cover, and framed on the face. A 16:9 source scaled to fill a 1080x960 box loses the sides; frame for that when shooting, or set crop_bias.
speaker._comment_crop_bias: Bias the crop upward so the eyeline sits in the upper third of the bottom half rather than dead centre.

layout._comment_graphics_mode: 'region' not 'overlay': a graphic here fills its half of the frame instead of floating over the speaker. Overlays are still anchored to {segment_id, offset_frames} and never to an absolute timeline frame.

captions_region._comment: The middle band. build_ass emits \pos at the centre point; the block grows symmetrically about the seam as lines are added. Wider than platforms.tiktok.safe_area_pct would allow on the right - legitimate here only because the band sits at 43-57 % height, above where the action rail begins.

_comment_hook: No separate hook card - the first graphic in the top half IS the hook. Give it the strongest line in the script and make sure it lands inside the first 1.5 s.
